skills.name: sound-design-auditory-hierarchy
skills.description: Three-level auditory hierarchy: foreground (conscious), midground (aware), background (subconscious). Manages audience attention through conscious layering of sound elements.

skills.name: sound-design-consistency
skills.description: Once a sound-image association is established, it must remain consistent throughout the film. Inconsistent sounds break audience trust and immersion.

skills.name: sound-design-contrast-drama
skills.description: Drama comes from contrast, not absolute values. Loud-soft, fast-slow, full-empty contrasts create tension. Constant loudness causes auditory fatigue.

skills.name: sound-design-diegetic-taxonomy
skills.description: Sound-image relationship taxonomy: on-screen, off-screen, non-diegetic, acousmatic. Classifies any film sound by its relationship to the story world.

skills.name: sound-design-energy-model
skills.description: Four-layer sound energy transformation model for film: physical, emotional, intellectual, ethical. Maps how sound travels from source to audience across technical, dramatic, aesthetic, and spiritual dimensions.

skills.name: sound-design-entrainment
skills.description: Human physiological rhythms (heartbeat, breathing, brainwaves) synchronize with external sound rhythms. Sound designers can use this to guide audience states.

skills.name: sound-design-expectation
skills.description: Sound's emotional power comes from building and violating expectations. Surprise requires prior setup; too-accurate prediction causes boredom.

skills.name: sound-design-less-is-more
skills.description: Use minimum sound elements for maximum impact. Let audience fill in gaps mentally. Counter-intuitive: removing sounds often increases emotional engagement.

skills.name: sound-design-listening-modes
skills.description: Four listening modes (reduced, causal, semantic, referential) for understanding how audiences perceive and interpret sounds. Enables conscious mode-switching for effective sound design.

skills.name: sound-design-music-story-parallel
skills.description: Music-story parallel structure: melody=character, harmony=setting, dissonance=conflict, rhythm=tempo. Maps musical elements to narrative elements for integrated sound design.

skills.name: sound-design-size-control
skills.description: Perceived size of sound sources can be controlled by changing playback speed. Slower = larger, faster = smaller. Combine with original speed for realism.

skills.name: sound-design-sonata-drama
skills.description: Sonata form maps to dramatic structure: exposition (setup) → development (conflict) → recapitulation (resolution). Mirrors Hero's Journey and three-act structure.

skills.name: sound-design-sync-illusion
skills.description: Audiences believe any sound synchronized with image IS the image's sound. Real sounds often have poor dramatic effect; substitute sources work better.
